name: Lina Barrett
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember losing my hometown vowels in my first interview.” Friday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Lina keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I was ashamed my language sounded provincial when I moved here. This is the first job letter I've listed it on.
appearance: Lina is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case, Lina holds eye contact until the other person has finished when listening.
personality: Lina reads little signals of discomfort very accurately and has an unfortunate habit of overruling people for their own good. The friends who say stop are the ones Lina trusts most.
agenda: To list the home language on a real application.
family: Carl Reeve is Lina’s cousin raised in the same household. Lina knows which ones can be shared. Carl keeps the photographs. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *An unfinished atlas*, Carl says, “I saved the atlas from the paper skip because its spine matched my coat.”
connections: Rain Yang. Training applications and job letters reveal two workers' long-hidden language skills.
